title: Robey’s Atlas — Historical map room
scope: Authentic archival map records. Historical map viewpoints are not current Indigenous boundaries. Link-only records distinguish uninspected images and metadata-only leads.

maps.title: Map of the Indian tribes of North America, about 1600 A.D. along the Atlantic, & about 1800 A.D. westwardly
maps.creator: Albert Gallatin; American Antiquarian Society
maps.credit: Albert Gallatin; Pendleton’s Lithography. David Rumsey Historical Map Collection, list no.3388.001. Digital image © Cartography Associates.

rights.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 2.0. Noncommercial reuse with attribution and share-alike terms.

maps.annotation: Gallatin assembled this map for an American Antiquarian Society publication in 1836. Its title distinguishes eastern depictions around 1600 from western depictions around 1800. Compare its historical naming and classifications with later maps; its labels do not define current communities or borders.

preview.alt: Authentic 1836 Gallatin map: North America with color-coded historical classifications and a printed key.
preview.changes: Archive-supplied small preview, unaltered full frame. No generated content. The larger image is available through the archive record.

inspection.scope: Read Rumsey’s full catalogue record and linked license; inspected the actual small map image. Fine labels require the archive viewer. The alternate LOC record was read as indexed text.

maps.creator: Unidentified Indigenous maker; colonial copy associated with Francis Nicholson
maps.dateNote: Guide dates presentation of the underlying Indigenous draught approximately 1721.
maps.credit: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division.

rights.statement: Reuse permitted unless an item-specific Rights Advisory states otherwise. No preview reproduced here.

maps.annotation: An archival reproduction preserves a copied network of communities and paths drawn from Indigenous knowledge. The conventional Catawba title does not establish the maker’s identity. Colonial annotations and multiple copying stages make its production history essential context for interpretation.

inspection.scope: Read the full indexed archive record and the archive guide; direct item access was blocked. Map image not viewed. Guide dates presentation of the underlying Indigenous draught approximately 1721.

rights.statement: Reuse permitted unless an item-specific Rights Advisory states otherwise. No preview reproduced here.

maps.annotation: This battlefield sketch credits Indigenous direction, while the catalog associates it with John Montrésor. That wording exposes a history of mediation and copying. It offers a focused example of Indigenous geographic knowledge entering a colonial military record, with its maker unnamed.

inspection.scope: Read the full indexed archive record and the archive guide; direct item access was blocked. Map image not viewed. Retain the catalog's uncertainty.

maps.annotation: A British colonial map of southern Quebec and neighboring borderlands, compiled from French surveys. maps.title: Linguistic Stocks of American Indians North of Mexico.
maps.creator: John Wesley Powell
maps.archive: University of Texas at Arlington Library / UNT Libraries, The Portal to Texas History
maps.credit: University of Texas at Arlington Library / UNT Libraries, The Portal to Texas History.

rights.statement: The item-specific page leaves copyright status undetermined and permits links. Do not embed this copy.

maps.annotation: Powell grouped North American Indigenous languages into the linguistic stocks used by nineteenth-century federal ethnology. Read this as a historical classification project, including its names and large colored areas, alongside language and community accounts. These areas do not establish present boundaries.

inspection.scope: Read item metadata, item-specific rights and IIIF manifest. Image opening failed; no visual claim.

maps.annotation: This Office of Indian Affairs map presents Indian Territory through federal administrative categories in 1889, with information about occupied lands, transfers and cessions. Its vocabulary belongs to that dated record. Examine federal mapping practices alongside the histories of the nations shown.
